name: Gambari Iskandarani (Garlicky Alexandrian Shrimp)

instructions.primary_message: In a 12- or 14-inch skillet, wide enough to hold shrimp in a single layer, heat oil over medium heat until shimmering. Add onion, bell pepper, and chile pepper and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, 3 to 5 minutes. Add garlic, cumin, coriander, paprika, and pepper and cook, stirring occasionally, until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Stir in tomatoes, tomato paste, and salt and cook, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened, about 2 minutes. Add water and bring to a simmer over medium-low heat. Cook until sauce thickens and tomatoes are completely softened, 3 to 5 minutes.

Add shrimp and butter and gently toss to coat. Cook until shrimp are pink and opaque throughout, 3 to 5 minutes. If sauce becomes too thick, add additional water, 1 tablespoon at a time, until sauce lightly coats shrimp.
Remove from heat and stir in lemon juice. Transfer to a serving platter and top with cilantro leaves and lemon wedges or slices. Serve immediately with bread or rice.

description: This easy Alexandrian shrimp simmers in a garlicky, warmly spiced tomato sauce for an easy seafood dinner that comes together in about 20 minutes.
notes:
Optional or for serving: Fresh cilantro leaves, for serving; Lemon wedges or slices, for serving; Flatbread such as pita or cooked rice, for serving

Notes: For instructions on deveining shell-on shrimp, see our tutorial, which explains multiple methods.If head-on shrimp are unavailable, you can make the dish with large, headless, shell-on shrimp in place of head-on shrimp.

Make-ahead and storage: Leftovers can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 4 days.
author: Nermine Mansour
